text:
Cassidy supports SB0248, permitting post-conviction petitions for those convicted under age 21
C. A. Tran
Rep. Kelly M. Cassidy (D-14th) voted Yes on SB0248, legislation that permits certain individuals convicted prior to age 21 to file post-conviction petitions. The vote occurred during the 104th General Assembly on May 31, 2026. The bill cleared the Illinois House by a 63-42 margin, as indicated by the Illinois House.
The official description for the measure reads: "CRIM PRO-POST-CONVICT PETITION."
The following summary relies on the bill's text and provides explanatory notes for clarity regarding its provisions.
In summary, SB0248 updates the Code of Criminal Procedure of 1963, allowing people convicted of felony crimes that took place before they were 21 to submit a subsequent post-conviction petition without being required to show cause if asserting their sentence breaches the Illinois Constitution's proportionate penalties clause. Under this law, petitioners are no longer obligated to demonstrate that they faced specific barriers in raising those claims in earlier legal proceedings. The act will take effect immediately once enacted.
The final action on SB0248 was recorded as 'Third Reading - Short Debate - Passed.'
Cassidy, elected to the Illinois State House in 2011, represents the 14th House District. She succeeded Harry Osterman.
Illinois legislation proceeds through a multi-phase legislative process that starts with bill introduction in either chamber, followed by committee hearings, debates, and votes from both the House and Senate, before consideration by the governor for passage or veto. The General Assembly convenes biennially, with only a portion of the numerous introduced bills making it into law each session.
